survivors.claim: The ratchet baseline lookup does a string-prefix match on the relative path instead of exact key equality, letting an unbaselined narrated file inherit an unrelated tracked file's baseline budget
survivors.impact: A new file with narration text can silently pass the gate by sharing a filename prefix with an existing tracked file, defeating the whole point of the ratchet that is supposed to freeze debt at zero growth
survivors.evidence: D6 (spec line 42): 'A scanned file passes iff its finding count <= its baseline count (absent path -> 0).' Code: const baseKey = Object.keys(baseline).find((k) => file.startsWith(k)). Executed repro: root with spec/scripts/x.js (no narration) and spec/scripts/x.js.evasion.js containing a comment '// 2026-09-02 previously used to be different'; baseline.json = {"spec/scripts/x.js": 5}; node comment-narration.js --root . --baseline baseline.json printed 'spec/scripts/x.js.evasion.js:2 [date,prior] ...' / '1 findings in 2 files' and exited 0 (should be 1, since x.js.evasion.js has no real baseline entry).
